THE ACTIVITY CUPBOARD

What shall we discover?

Nine free activities. Everyday materials. Plenty of room to make them your own.

The Grow a Bean activity collection

01How to Grow a Bean

Set up a tiny science project with a grown-up. Make a prediction, then check your bean each day.

Draw · Type · Save02My Plant Diary

Look at the same bean over several days. Record what you actually see—even if nothing has changed yet.

Draw · Type · Save03How Tall Is Your Plant?

Once your seedling is planted in soil, measure its height and compare your records.

Draw · Type · Save04Parts of My Plant

Look for a seed, root, stem and leaf. Draw each part, name it and describe what it does.

Draw · Type · Save05My Bean Leaf

Become a leaf detective. Look gently and leave the leaf attached to the plant.

Draw · Type · Save06Life Cycle of a Bean Plant

Follow a bean from seed to new seeds. Use the picture cards, then explain the changes in your own words.

Draw · Type · Save07Decorate Your Plant

Design an imaginary plant with leaves, flowers, pods and seeds. Draw on screen or use the printable cutouts.

Draw · Type · Save

Write, trace & draw on screen.

A space to practise letters, numbers and your name with a finger, stylus or mouse.

Try handwriting ↗

9 activities to explore

Grow a bean

Ages 6–1220 min + daily check-ins

Watch roots and shoots appear, then draw the changes in your own bean diary.

Make a shape collage

Ages 3–825 min

Tear, arrange and layer colourful paper to make a picture that is entirely your own.

Make a repeating pattern

Ages 3–815 min

Turn big paper shapes into repeating patterns and challenge someone to find your rule.

Draw a story map

Ages 6–1230 min

Invent a character, give them a problem and draw their way to an ending.

Make a sound map

Ages 3–1215 min

Listen from one safe spot and draw a map of the sounds around you.

Build a paper bridge

Ages 6–1230 min

Test how folding changes a paper bridge, then improve your design with a fair comparison.

Sink or Float?

Ages 4–720–30 minutes

Test everyday objects in water, record what happens and redesign a foil boat.

My Weather Journal

Ages 4–75–10 minutes a day

Observe the sky, keep a weather diary, choose an outfit and build a toy shelter.

Mixing Colours

Ages 4–720–30 minutes

Predict paint mixtures, record your results, match colour cards and invent your own shade.
